1	# Creating a command
2	
3	Commands are declared with `defineCommand`, `defineOption` and `defineArgument`, on top of `cliparse`. Options and arguments are validated and parsed by [Zod](https://zod.dev) schemas, and their types flow into the handler. The reasons behind this design are explained in [ADR 0001](../adr/adr-0001-rework-file-structure.md).
4	
5	Before writing a command, look at a similar one and copy its naming, file layout, output format and error messages. `src/commands/drain/` is a good example of a command group with shared arguments and options.
6	
7	## Example
8	
9	A fictional `clever coffee brew <blend>` subcommand, part of a `coffee` group (neither exists in the CLI). The `<blend>` argument is shared by several `coffee` subcommands, so it lives in `coffee.args.js`:
10	
11	```js
12	// src/commands/coffee/coffee.args.js
13	import { z } from 'zod';
14	import { defineArgument } from '../../lib/define-argument.js';
15	
16	export const blendArg = defineArgument({
17	  schema: z.string().regex(/^[a-z0-9-]+$/, 'Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes'),
18	  description: 'Blend of coffee',
19	  placeholder: 'blend',
20	});
21	```
22	
23	`--shots`, `--milk` and `--topping` are only used by this subcommand, so they are defined inline. `--format` comes from `global.options.js`:
24	
25	```js

27	import { z } from 'zod';
28	import { brewCoffee } from '../../clever-client/coffee.js';
29	import { defineCommand } from '../../lib/define-command.js';
30	import { defineOption } from '../../lib/define-option.js';
31	import { Logger } from '../../logger.js';
32	import { sendToApi } from '../../models/send-to-api.js';
33	import { humanJsonOutputFormatOption } from '../global.options.js';
34	import { blendArg } from './coffee.args.js';
35	
36	export const coffeeBrewCommand = defineCommand({
37	  description: 'Brew a coffee',
38	  since: null,
39	  options: {
40	    shots: defineOption({
41	      name: 'shots',
42	      schema: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(4).default(1),
43	      description: 'Number of espresso shots',
44	      aliases: ['s'],
45	      placeholder: 'shots',
46	    }),
47	    milk: defineOption({
48	      name: 'milk',

50	      description: 'Kind of milk',
51	      placeholder: 'milk',
52	    }),
53	    toppings: defineOption({

I haven't written any code yet. The Clever Cloud API can't test a recipient before the drain exists, so the command can't work as you described it.

**What the API offers.** I checked the endpoints in `CleverCloud/clever-client.js` on master. None of them appear in this repo's `src/clever-client/drains.js` yet.

- **`POST /v4/drains/organisations/{ownerId}/resources/{resourceId}/drains/{drainId}/check`**: Clever Cloud's servers probe the recipient and return the result (`ok`, `code`, `message`, plus HTTP or TCP details). It needs the ID of an existing drain. It also sends a sample log line to the recipient, so running it twice sends two lines.
- **`GET …/drains/{drainId}/test-command`**: returns a shell command the user can run to send a sample payload to the recipient themselves. It also needs an existing drain, and nothing is contacted by the API.

I found no endpoint that takes a URL and credentials without a drain.

**Something to fix in the docs.** `docs/contributing/commands.md:167` uses `clever drain check` and `src/commands/drain/drain.check.command.js` as a real example. Neither exists in the repo.

**Options:**

1. **`clever drain check <drain-id>`**, using the `/check` endpoint, with the same `--app`/`--alias`/`--addon` options as `drain get`, plus `--format json`. It would print whether the recipient answered and the error detail if not. To test before relying on a drain, users would create it, check it, and remove it if the check fails. This is the only version the current API supports, and I'd recommend it.
2. **Test the URL and credentials from the user's machine**, without the API. I'd advise against this: it tests the user's network, not Clever Cloud's. A recipient behind a firewall could pass the check and still fail as a drain.
3. **Ask the API team** for a pre-creation endpoint (for example `POST …/drains/check` taking the same body as `create`), and build the command once it exists.

Which do you want? For option 1, the repo's rules also require an issue to reference (`Closes #N`). `gh` isn't logged in here, so please give me the issue number or log in so I can draft one.
